items.title: StepFun previewed a 600B MoE model
items.oneliner: Step 5 Preview packs 600B parameters and long context. Chinese frontier labs are still closing the gap fast.

items.title: Open weights raised the security alarm
items.oneliner: GLM 5.3-flash pushed researchers to call for a one-year security sprint. Capability diffusion is outrunning defenses.

items.title: HEIF parsing became an RCE risk
items.oneliner: HEIF Heist shows crafted HEIC and AVIF files can trigger memory corruption. Your image pipeline is now attack surface.

items.title: Model weights got an exfiltration playbook
items.oneliner: Exfiltrate Your Weights turns stolen checkpoints into a copy-paste workflow. Model security is now a practical ops problem.

items.title: OpenAI paywall evidence got uglier
items.oneliner: NYT lawsuit evidence says OpenAI staff celebrated paywall bypassing. Fair use arguments look weaker when intent is documented.

items.title: Spain blocked Archive.today without a court
items.oneliner: Spain ordered ISPs to block Archive.today and mirrors administratively. Content enforcement is getting faster and less judicial.

items.title: RSA-896 was factored at last
items.oneliner: RSA-896 fell, marking another public milestone for integer factorization. Legacy crypto assumptions keep aging in public.

items.title: Notion explained its CRDT rewrite
items.oneliner: Notion replaced last-write-wins with CRDTs for block editing. Real-time collaboration is finally being engineered, not hand-waved.

items.title: Typst took another step toward LaTeX
items.oneliner: Typst 0.15 added variable fonts and stronger technical-doc support. The LaTeX replacement story keeps getting more credible.

items.title: io_uring may cut worker-thread overhead
items.oneliner: Jens Axboe's io_uring RFC tackles blocking paths without punting to workers. Linux async I/O could get materially cheaper.
